hints.title: Group by Employee
hints.text: Aggregate over each employee identifier to extract their single latest salary record.

hints.title: Maximum Salary as Latest
hints.text: Select max salary for each emp_id along with firstname, lastname, and department_id.

hints.title: Order Output
hints.text: Group by emp_id, firstname, lastname, department_id and order by emp_id in ascending order.

hints.title: Aggregation Query Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    emp_id,
    firstname,
    lastname,
    MAX(salary) AS salary,
    department_id
FROM Salary
GROUP BY emp_id, firstname, lastname, department_id
ORDER BY emp_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting groups by employee identifier
complexity.notes: Group-by aggregation computes maximum salary per employee.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row-by-row subquery without grouping produces Cartesian overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hash aggregate table sorts unique employee identifiers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Groups by employee attributes and calculates max salary cleanly.

    department_id

import pandas as pd

def find_latest_salaries(salary: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = salary.groupby(['emp_id', 'firstname', 'lastname', 'department_id'])['salary'].max().reset_index()
    return df.sort_values(by='emp_id')[['emp_id', 'firstname', 'lastname', 'salary', 'department_id']]
